source.display_title: 07/24/2026 - Giulian Carcioppolo x Richard Claessen — Lost

call.sequence_note: Explicit follow-up to a prior call: 'I think I said it last time as well' and 'we already have done that 100' — a $100 deposit had already been taken on the previous call. The $6,000 offer was presented before this call.

prospect.name: Giulian Vito Carcioppolo
prospect.occupation: Manager at the family Italian restaurant (Gabriele's Italian Restaurant); working reduced hours since his accident
prospect.family_status: Long-term girlfriend he intends to propose to; parents and siblings are financially supporting him through his recovery
prospect.training_background: Training on his own in the days before the call — 'in the past two days, three days, I've been doing kettlebells' — plus daily morning stretching; also in structured physical/speech therapy
prospect.medical: Recovering from a serious accident affecting speech, mobility, shoulder and brain function; has been working with up to three therapists weekly, currently one because of summer breaks; large ongoing hospital, therapy and medication costs

signals: Explicitly framing training as recovery from an accident — rep: 'this injury happened, the accident occurred, and you use that as fuel'
Wants shape/form back and shoulder function restored: 'I was interested in my shape, my form, and about my shoulder and the accident in general'
High personal drive but the hard season (accident, medical costs, reduced work) is the controlling constraint

goals.text: Improve his physical shape and form again after the accident
Rehabilitate his shoulder and overall mobility
Learn to keep training consistently with kettlebells alongside his therapy

pains.text: Ongoing accident recovery — speech, mobility and shoulder still limited
Brain health and medical recovery consume both his attention and his money; he ranks them above training
Spending more than he earns; family is covering his costs, no defined monthly surplus
Not working his normal hours at the family restaurant because of the accident

objections.raw_quote: right now, for that $6,000 for like six months, it's, it's not going to be able to happen, you know.
objections.rep_response: Acknowledged and validated it, isolated money as the only blocker ('it sounds like that's the only thing that's stopping you at the moment, right?'), then pivoted straight to a lower-priced Primal University tier rather than working the money play through.

objections.raw_quote: I don't really have a budget. I just know that I'm spending more than I have right now. And people are helping me. My family, my parents, my siblings, helping me.
objections.rep_response: Probed monthly leftover and cash available now, accepted that there was no fixed number, and did not pursue credit, savings or investments.

objections.raw_quote: It's something I would be interested in. Like I said, I would have to think about it, because right now my finance is not where I want to be.
objections.rep_response: Did not run the think-about-it play. Tested $200/month once, took the no, and then withdrew the offer himself — 'let's just stay in contact... we'll send back the hundreds'.

objections.raw_quote: I just don't, I don't feel comfortable, like, putting more money, you know, right now, because I know things are going to change... I don't think I'm comfortable doing like 200 a month, and then, you know, having like a fixed rate
objections.rep_response: Accepted immediately, made one more probe on cash available now, then closed the conversation out and offered to refund the $100 already paid.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Primal University at $200/month or $1,000 paid for six months, with the $1,000 credited toward future one-on-one coaching. The rep then restated the monthly plan as '200 a month, paid over six times, and then it's 1,200 in total for the six months', which contradicts the $1,000 six-month price he had just quoted.

evidence: Declined the $6,000 six-month program outright: 'it's not going to be able to happen'
Declined the $200/month downsell: 'I don't think I'm comfortable doing like 200 a month'
Rep withdrew and refunded the prior $100 deposit: 'We'll send back the hundreds, get that back'

Counter-evidence: the relationship stayed warm and both sides agreed to keep checking in — 'when I have my finances more is balanced, I would like to get involved with the 200 a month' — so this could be reopened later
Counter-evidence: no explicit 'no' to the company, only to the money; the rep framed it as a pause, not a loss
outcome.next_step: Rep refunds the $100 deposit within a day or two, prospect follows Trevor's YouTube and keeps training, rep checks in every few weeks until finances improve.

notable.note: Pricing deviation and a refund. A previously collected $100 deposit was returned on this call. A non-standard Primal University tier was offered at $200/month or $1,000/6 months, and the rep then misquoted the plan total as $1,200 for the same six months. The rep also disqualified on ethics rather than pressing — 'the last thing that we want to do is put someone in an even worse financial position' — which is defensible but means no objection play was run at all. Prospect is mid-recovery from a serious accident with brain involvement; medical spend dwarfs the offer.

quality.notes: Frequent inversions. At 00:00:33 the prospect's block opens with the rep's question 'How does it look like for you?'; at 00:04:49 a rep line ('the cards that you've been dealt and that needs a workaround') is attributed to the prospect; at 00:11:09 and 00:14:16 rep and prospect lines are merged into single blocks. Role was read from content throughout.
